correctness.rationale: At depth zero only color matters, including the single empty assignment when p=0. Inductively characteristic formulas express the presence of every specified child type and forbid all others, using the stated empty Boolean conventions. Each specified type needs a different child, and tree children cannot share vertices. Equality in the resulting order lower bound requires exactly one child and an inductively unique minimum representative for every member of the chosen child-type set. This yields the product, the type-count recurrence, and the largest exponent from taking all children. Subset complementation gives symmetry about (M_h+1)/2 and the two extreme coefficients, also valid when they coincide at depth zero. Sorted positive weights with no missing order satisfy a_i<=1+sum_{j<i}a_j, so appending a weight gives two overlapping or adjacent integer intervals of subset sums. Uniform types give independent fair selections of the predecessor types, yielding the exact variance recurrence and positive variance at h>=1. The centered summands have second and third absolute moments w^2/4 and w^3/8. With A=sum w=N(M+1)/2 and B=sum w^2, the Berry–Esseen moment ratio is bounded by M/sqrt(B)<=M sqrt(N)/A<=2/sqrt(N). For the Hoeffding bound, B<=MA and the new maximum is 1+A, so 2(1+A)^2/B>=N. The preceding N grows without bound, as does M, proving both limiting assertions. Independent bounded enumeration found, among other cases, all 16 atom-free depth-three types, maximum 11 and successive multiplicities 1,1,1,2,2,2,2,2,1,1,1, with one minimum tree per type.
residual_risks: The finite replay supplements the all-depth proof. The original checker's example moment calculations use floating-point division and accumulation, not a rational-arithmetic moment certificate; the proof of the moment identities is exact.

The original MathNet source could not be read in the bounded attempts; the applicability of the 0.56 bound is corroborated by the non-iid use in Pinelis. No optimal approximation constant, graph-relative minimum or counting modality is claimed.

value.rationale: The whole range and distribution of the smallest useful tree representatives gives information that counting theories or giving only a worst-case upper bound cannot provide. Gap-freeness settles exactly which optimal witness orders can occur. The quantitative limit separates typical size from extremal size across a canonical uniform ensemble, with nonasymptotic errors despite the rapid growth in type count. These are natural questions about bounded modal succinctness, not a census of arbitrary instances or a novelty claim for the generic inequalities.
residual_risks: The utility is for the tree-relative uniform-type ensemble, not uniform random trees or unrestricted Kripke model compression.
